thread:
alex: Heads-up — after yesterday's RBAC role_map rollout a handful of EU users are still able to access Dedicated resources even though SCIM shows they'd been deprovisioned. No deprov audit entries showing up in the logs. Anyone seen this before?

maria: huh. Which audit stream are you checking? infra-audit or the new audit-shipper?

alex: audit-shipper (kafka -> gcs) first, then ran a direct query against infra-audit (internal ES). Nothing for the user ids that were deprovisioned at 03:12 UTC. SCIM shows PATCH /scim/v2/Users/xxxxx -> {"active": false} at 03:12 and returned 200.

ops-bot: Incident created: #INC-2026-312 (ticket open, low->sev2 pending triage) :rotating_light:

jordan: quick question — did we rotate any KMS aliases or rekey the audit-shipper service account around that window? We rotated a customer KMS alias at 03:10 for other maintenance.

alex: yes, there was a KMS alias rekey at 03:09 for the audit-shipper alias (we were supposed to do it in canary first, but it hit production).

maria: that could explain missing audit entries if the shipper couldn't decrypt old envelopes. Do we have shipper logs?

alex: pasted shipper stderr snippet:
```
2026-03-19T03:12:18Z shipper ERROR decrypt failed: AccessDeniedException: caller not authorized to decrypt with key alias/alias/audit-shipper
2026-03-19T03:12:18Z shipper WARN dropping envelope id=env_3e7f because decrypt failed
```

sam: oof. So SCIM patches succeeded but audit-shipper dropped the deprov event because encryption/decryption failed. That would leave runtime caches or authorization caches out of sync if we rely on audit-stream-driven invalidation.

ida-security: Confirming hypothesis: our runtime invalidation of RBAC cache listens to the audit topic. If the shipper dropped the message, the cache never saw the deprov event — meaning the user retains permissions until TTL or manual purge.

maria: any sign SCIM retried or any retry errors from the scim-proxy?

alex: scim-proxy logs show the PATCH response 200 from IdP and internalService returned 204, no retries. But we also saw a few 5xx from scim-proxy earlier at 03:11 which coincided with the rekey window:
```
2026-03-19T03:11:56Z scim-proxy ERROR upstream write timeout
2026-03-19T03:12:00Z scim-proxy INFO PATCH /scim/v2/Users/xxxxx response=200 latency=340ms
```

jordan: so timeline: KMS alias rekey at 03:09 -> some decrypt errors in shipper -> scim-proxy chattiness at 03:11 but PATCH still returned 200 -> audit-shipper drops envelope at 03:12 -> runtime RBAC cache doesn't see deprov -> users keep access. Makes sense.

sam: mitigation? Can we replay the SCIM events or reconstruct deprov audit entries and re-publish to audit topic?

ida-security: immediate actions: 1) rollback alias change to previous key if still available (hotfix) 2) enable shipper fallback that writes raw envelopes to S3 bucket for manual replay 3) run a reconcile script to force in-memory RBAC cache invalidation for affected tenant ids.

alex: I did a partial rollback of role_map (canary) which reduced new hits, and asked infra to re-add old KMS alias to the policy. That stopped new decrypt failures. Still need to backfill the missing deprov events.

maria: I'll open a provisioning ticket to run a one-off reconcile (scim -> id store) for the affected tenant ids, and export SCIM change logs for 03:00-03:30 UTC.

jordan: I'll pull KMS CloudTrail for the alias and the shipper's IAM policy change history. Also will get Kafka offsets for the audit topic to confirm which envelopes were dropped.

ops-bot: @jordan assigned as oncall for #INC-2026-312

jordan: on it. Quick note: to replay we can reconstruct a minimal deprov envelope and publish to kafka with the original timestamp header. But we should add a sentinel in the shipper to alert on decrypt failures immediately (right now it's WARN only).

sam: agree — add an alert on decrypt failure rate > 1/min. Also add a healthcheck that ensures shipper can decrypt a recent test envelope after KMS rotations.

ida-security: long-term follow-ups: - make RBAC runtime fall back to authoritative SCIM/Provisioning for final decision when audit stream gap detected - add end-to-end integration test covering KMS rotations during deploy windows - improve shipper visibility (structured errors + metrics).

alex: for forensics, we need a list of all users that were deprovisioned between 03:05-03:20 UTC across EU region. Maria + Jordan, can you coordinate for data export and attach to the incident?

maria: yes, will attach export to ticket and ping legal for any compliance flag.

jordan: pulling logs now, will post a short timeline and a replay plan in #incidents.

ida-security: final note — this is a good example of two low-risk ops (role_map change + KMS rotation) overlapping to create a data-plane gap. Let's add a scheduling guard: block KMS alias rotates during RBAC rollouts for the same tenant for 24h. :no_entry:

alex: thanks all — running the reconcile job now, will update when we confirm affected sessions purged. :white_check_mark:
